stem: A driver’s “safe speed” is the speed at which he can just brake to a halt in 30 m. On a dry road his safe speed is 20 m/s. It starts to snow and the coefficient of friction drops to half its dry value. What is his safe speed now (m/s, nearest integer)? (Neglect reaction time.)

A horizontal force of 10 N is necessary to just hold a block stationary against a wall. The coefficient of friction between the block and the wall is 0.2, the weight of the block is [figure: the 10 N force pushes the block horizontally into a vertical wall] (A) 2 N (B) 20 N (C) 50 N (D) 100 N

A cart of mass M has a block of mass ‘m’ attached to it as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between the block and cart is μ. The minimum acceleration of the cart so that the block m does not fall is: [figure: the block m is stuck to the outer vertical right-hand (leading) face of the cart with nothing beneath it; the cart rolls on a horizontal floor] (A) g/μ (B) μ/g (C) μg (D) Mμg/m

A 10 kg block is placed on an inclined plane with an inclination of 45°. The coefficient of friction between the block and the plane is 0.3. What is the minimum force parallel to the plane required to keep the block at rest? (A) 50 N (B) 60 N (C) 80 N (D) 100 N

A heavy uniform chain lies on a horizontal table top. If the coefficient of friction between the chain and the table surface is 0.25, then the maximum fraction of the length of the chain that can hang over on edge of the table is : (A) 20% (B) 25% (C) 35% (D) 15%

What is the maximum value of the force F such that the block shown in the arrangement, does not move? [Figure: block of mass m = √3 kg on a rough horizontal floor, μ = 1/(2√3); F is applied at 60° below the horizontal, pressing the block down and forward; take g = 10 m/s²] (A) 20 N (B) 10 N (C) 12 N (D) 15 N

Find, the distance travelled by block if μ K = V 0 t/2 and initial velocity of block is V 0 ? [Figure: a block of mass M sliding on a rough horizontal surface with velocity V 0 to the right] (A) infinite (B) 4V 0 /(3√g) (C) V 0 ²/g (D) 2V 0 /g

Minimum force required to keep a block of mass 10 kg at rest against a rough vertical wall is F 0 . If a force F 0 /2 is applied then find the acceleration of the block in m/s 2 . [Figure: a horizontal force F presses the 10 kg block into the wall; μ = 0.5; take g = 10 m/s 2 ]

key: D a A becomes constant (horizontal); a B rises more steeply
stem: A block B is placed on block A. The mass of block B is less than the mass of block A. Friction exists between the blocks, whereas the ground on which block A is placed is smooth. A horizontal force F, increasing linearly with time, begins to act on B. The accelerations a A and a B of blocks A and B are plotted against t. The correctly plotted graph is (A) common line, then a A horizontal while a B keeps the same slope (B) two separate lines from the origin, a B steeper (C) common line, then both rise, a A with a smaller slope (D) common line, then a A horizontal and a B rising steeply

Block B of mass 100 kg rests on a rough surface of friction coefficient μ = 1/3. A rope is tied to block B as shown (rope leaves B at 37° above the horizontal, passes over a fixed pulley and hangs vertically; boy A of 25 kg holds the other end). The maximum acceleration with which boy A of 25 kg can climb on the rope without making the block move is (A) 4g/3 (B) g/3 (C) g/2 (D) 3g/4

Block A of mass m and block B of mass 2m are placed on a fixed triangular wedge by means of a massless, inextensible string and a frictionless pulley as shown. The wedge is inclined at 45° to the horizontal on both sides. The coefficient of friction between block A and the wedge is 2/3 and that between block B and the wedge is 1/3. If the blocks A and B are released from rest, the acceleration of A is ____.

A block rests on a rough inclined plane making an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is 0.8. If the frictional force on the block is 10 N, the mass of the block (in kg) is (take g = 10 m/s 2 ) (A) 2.0 (B) 4.0 (C) 1.6 (D) 2.5

A horizontal force of 10 N is necessary to just hold a block stationary against a wall. The coefficient of friction between the block and the wall is 0.2, the weight of the block is [Figure: the 10 N force pushes the block horizontally into a vertical wall.] (A) 2 N (B) 20 N (C) 50 N (D) 100 N

Two blocks A and B of masses 6 kg and 3 kg rest on a smooth horizontal surface as shown in the figure. If coefficient of friction between A and B is 0.4, the maximum horizontal force which can make them move without separation is [figure: B (3 kg) sits on top of A (6 kg); the force F is applied horizontally to the lower block A] (A) 72 N (B) 40 N (C) 36 N (D) 20 N

A cart of mass M has a block of mass ‘m’ attached to it as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between the block and cart is μ. The minimum acceleration of the cart so that the block m does not fall is : [figure: block m is held against the front (leading) vertical face of the cart, nothing beneath it; the cart moves on a horizontal floor] (A) g/μ (B) μ/g (C) μg (D) Mμg/m

A block of mass 1 kg is placed over a plank of mass 2 kg. The length of the plank is 2 m. Coefficient of friction between the block and the plank is 0.5 and the ground over which plank is frictionless. A constant force F = 30 N is applied on the plank in horizontal direction. The time after which the block will separate from the plank is (g = 10 m/s²) [Figure: the 1 kg block sits at the front (right) end of the 2 m plank; F = 30 N pulls the plank to the right.] (A) 0.73 s (B) 1.2 s (C) 0.62 s (D) 1.6 s
